text.p: French doctors threatened to stop work on October 17 and leave their telephones off the hook for one night on Thursday to protest against plans to cut medical spending to trim the losses of the state welfare system.

Three unions claiming to represent two thirds of the country's doctors called for the October 17 stoppage, coinciding with a public sector strike against the government's austerity drive to join the European single currency in 1999.
Doctors "have become scapegoats for a society in crisis... They are blamed for the current crisis of Social Security," the unions said.
"This is a warning: we're being attacked from all sides and we're fed up," said Dinorino Caberera, head of the Union of Independent Doctors SML.
The conservative government is trying to rein in soaring spending by the French, who are generously reimbursed for their medical expenses by the state.

In a connected protest, five unions representing most general practitioners called on members to refuse to make night-time home visits on Thursday-Friday after the government said they would be entitled to extra payment only between 9 p.m. and 7 a.m, instead of 8 p.m. to 8 a.m. as now.

Unions say about half of the country's 55,000 general practitioners take turns for night duty. Doctors charge 300 francs ($60) for nightime home calls compared with 135 francs ($27) for daytime calls.

The government decision is part of a package of measures to trim the snowballing losses of the state welfare system as it struggles to cut the deficit in order to join a European single currency in 1999.
